```

```

Actually after our edit, the order is possibly out of sequence: We inserted // === UPDATE and // === RENDER before // === INPUT (which we previously had). The startLoop tick now calls update and render each frame.

But why canvas blank? Possibly player coordinates are off-screen? The player initial x is canvas.width/2 (400) and y is canvas.height - 30 (570). Player drawn with radius 8 at (400,570). Player visible region is correct. The background drawn at start of render with fillRect to set background. Then they draw the player and score.

But initial render draws fine.

However maybe player hasn't defined in global scope before startLoop? It is defined in reset (set player etc.). reset is called from boot and also from reset event which calls startLoop. So tick will start after startLoop schedule.

But within tick, after try-catch we call update and render; check that we have defined update and render before startLoop? In code, startLoop defined earlier (line 78...), update defined later lines 96-100, render defined later lines 103-119. Since functions are hoisted, they can be referenced before they are defined. But we need to ensure that script line numbers: startLoop defined earlier than update/render? Actually code had startLoop earlier at line 78-94; update defined at line 96-100; render at 103-119. That's fine.

Now why canvas still blank? Could be that render using ctx.fillRect with background overwrites player each frame? That's intended: first clear then draw player. So not blank.

Maybe we are not starting loop because we removed the call to render inside tick earlier but called update/render only if we succeeded. That should work.

Maybe page blank due to not calling requestAnimationFrame after tick? It does loopId = requestAnimationFrame(tick); fine.

But maybe error in code after startLoop: In tick, we use `ctx.clearRect` earlier, but now we added update/render before catch block? Wait we placed update/render inside try block after clearing -- we added update/render between after `lastTime = now;` and before catch? Actually we inserted at line:

```
try {
  const dt = Math.min((now - lastTime) / 1000, 0.1);
  lastTime = now;

  // Update game state and render
  update(dt);
  render();
} catch...
```

We removed clearRect? Actually original tick had clearRect inside try before our edit. The old code: inside try { ... ctx.clearRect(...) }. We replaced the block, but we didn't keep `ctx.clearRect`. Did we remove it? Let's verify old snippet: we replaced oldString which included clearRect line. The newString includes update/render but no clearRect. So now we have no clearing step. However render itself draws background fillRect; that covers entire canvas each frame. So it is fine. Not causing blank.

But perhaps we haven't added any code to draw hazards and portal; but blank canvas may still have just background and player drawn; but maybe player is hidden behind something? Could be that cursor draws but maybe player coordinates are off-screen due to canvas coordinates? No.

Update uses dt and score; no errors.

But there may be other sections missing calling render/ update for each frame? Already done.

Maybe the issue is that `phase` variable is never set to "playing"? Reset sets phase = "playing". Good.

But maybe we forgot to call `reset` on boot? At blink boot we call reset() at line 136. Yes.

Now the blank canvas could be because we changed config constants but not used anywhere else: we didn't use PLAYER_SCREEN_X, etc., but that's fine.

`beep` function defined earlier after BOOT? Actually we inserted beep in audio section before boot (that's before reset). That should be fine.

Now after we added update/render calls, maybe we forgot to call `render` on initial tick after resetting? The tick schedule waits for next animation frame; the first render occurs after ~16ms. That's fine; but even if not, the canvas will remain blank until then.
